chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from al-Hasan ibn Sadaqa, who said:
Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: 'Have a midday nap, for Allah feeds the fasting one and quenches him in his sleep.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of taking a midday nap while fasting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) encourages the practice of *qailulah* (midday nap) to conserve energy during fasting, linking it to a divine promise of sustenance and drink during sleep. This tradition highlights the spiritual and physical benefits of rest in Islamic asceticism, reflecting the Shia emphasis on balancing bodily needs with worship. The narration underscores the mercy of Allah in providing for the fasting believer even in their repose.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Mansour Bin Al Abbas, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Al Hassan Bin Sadaqa who said,
‘Abu Al Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Have a midday nap, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Feeds the Fasting-one and Quenches him in his sleep’.
en.sarwar: 14. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Mansur ibn al-‘Abbas from ‘Amr ibn Sa‘id from al-Hassan ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “
Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Rest in the form of a short nap between sunrise and noontime; Allah gives food and water to a fasting person during his sleep.”’
